summary: The command line always works in one folder at a time. pwd shows it, ls lists its contents, and cd moves to another folder.
notes: The prompt student@linux:~$ shows your user name, the computer name, and the folder you are in.
~ is a short name for your home folder, here /home/student.
cd with no folder name takes you home.
pitfall: Folder names are case-sensitive on Linux. cd CS fails with No such file or directory when the folder is named cs.
